title: Turnover or Hot Pocket, Pizza Pocket, Meat

content.title: About
content.content: A turnover (also called a hot pocket or pizza pocket) is a ready‑to‑heat baked product, usually filled with meat, cheese and tomato sauce. It is a small sealed pastry with the ingredients baked inside the dough, creating a juicy and flavorful snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Turnovers first appeared in the United States in the 1970s as a quick way to make a hot sandwich in a microwave.
In Russia similar items are often called “pizza‑pocket” and are sold in chain fast‑food stores.
The dough is typically made from wheat flour, water, yeast and a small amount of fat, giving it a soft yet slightly crisp texture after heating.
Fillings vary from classic beef and cheese to chicken, ham, vegetables, and even vegetarian versions.
Turnovers can be stored frozen for up to 12 months without loss of quality.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The meat filling provides a substantial amount of complete protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Energy provision
items.content: Turnovers contain carbohydrates and fats, offering a quick source of energy.

items.title: Iron content
items.content: Meat is rich in iron, which is essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The product includes B12, B6 and niacin, supporting metabolic processes.

items.title: Convenience and portability
items.content: Turnovers are easy to heat in a microwave and take on the go, fitting an active lifestyle.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Ready‑made items often contain a lot of salt, which may be undesirable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Meat and cheese fillings can be high in saturated fats, which should be limited in the diet.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The product may contain dairy, gluten and soy, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Thermal safety
items.content: Insufficiently heated turnover may harbor pathogenic bacteria, so follow heating time recommendations.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Heat the turnover in a microwave for 1‑2 minutes or bake in an oven until golden. Serve hot, optionally adding fresh vegetables, sauce or herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. After thawing, cook immediately and do not store more than 24 hours in the refrigerator.
